---
title: "Sequencing in Pharmacology & Toxicology"
subtitle: "An interactive, browser-based lecture course"
page-layout: article
---

This course template demonstrates how a modern sequencing-focused pharmacology and
toxicology lecture can be delivered entirely through an ordinary web browser — no
software installation, no account, no computational runtime. Open a lecture link,
follow along on the projected screen, and interact with the same activities on your
own device when the instructor invites you to.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**This is a demonstration template.** The scientific content, gene names, and datasets
throughout this site are small and **fictional**, used only to illustrate the
interactive mechanics. An instructor will replace them with authentic course material.
:::

## Lectures

::: {.lecture-grid}

::: {.lecture-card}
### [What Can Sequencing Tell Us in Pharmacology and Toxicology?](lectures/lecture-01-showcase.html)
A complete demonstration lecture (~18 slides) alternating conventional teaching
slides with hands-on interactive activities: signature matching, dynamic
clustering, pathway construction, mixture simulation, dose-response modeling,
experimental design, PCA, and spatial resolution.

[Open lecture →](lectures/lecture-01-showcase.html){.btn-lecture}
:::

::: {.lecture-card}
### [Blank Lecture Template](lectures/lecture-02-template.html)
A skeleton lecture with the same slide setup, navigation, and attribution
footer as the demonstration lecture, ready to be filled in with real content.
Intended for instructors building a new lecture, not for students.

[Open template →](lectures/lecture-02-template.html){.btn-lecture}
:::

:::

## Explore activities on their own

Every interactive activity used in the lectures can also be opened directly, outside
of any slide deck, from the [**Activity Gallery**](activities/index.html) — useful for
self-study, review after class, or previewing an activity before building a lecture
around it.

## For instructors

See the [Resources page](resources.qmd) for setup, editing, and deployment
documentation, including how to replace the fictional example data with real course
content.
